messages:
Alex: Taking over evening on-call, I'm primary for the next 8h. Any active P1/P2s I should know about? I'll be on pager and slack.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT SUMMARY (open):
- incident: infra/gpu-pool-throttle
- severity: P2
- first alerted: 1934565600
- current status: degraded throughput, autoscale partially failing
- assigned: Priya (driver), Mike (secondary)
- impacted customers: batch inference jobs (some retries), a few dedicated tenants seeing higher latency
Priya: hey Alex -- Priya here, still driving the throttle issue. Right now we've pushed a temporary autoscale policy patch (rollback ready). Observability shows queue depth improving but some nodes still in pending state.
Alex: thanks. Priya, do you want me to be comms owner or should Sara take that? I can field NRR updates if needed.
Priya: can you take comms for the first hour? I'm focused on the kube node drain/replace flow. If it flares back hands off to Mike after 23:00.
Mike: happy to take over after 23:00. Heads up I'm expecting a 30m break at 22:40 for dinner (covered by Alex).
Alex: noted. I'll post a short customer-facing status in #customer-impact and update the incident page. Draft below, lemme know edits: "We are investigating elevated inference latency for batch jobs. Engineering is applying autoscale mitigations; no data loss. We'll update in 15 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sara: I'll standby as comms backup — if you need a clear message for external sla-sensitive customers I can craft one. Also cross-post to #dedicated-customers if you want.
Alex: please do, Sara, only if Priya confirms we need external comms. For the runbook pointers:
- Playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/infra/autoscale-throttle (see step 3 rollback)
- Quick commands I ran earlier:```kubectl get pods -n inference -l role=worker -o wide
kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/maintenance=true```
Priya: progress update at 1934567905 -- queue depth down 40%, a few nodes still provisioning. I'm going to trigger a controlled node replace in the pool in 5m. If the node replace doesn't reduce pending to <5, we'll cut the canary policy to 1 replica.
Alex: thanks. I'll keep the customer status updates cadence: initial (now), update (15m), escalation (45m) if not resolved.
Mike: FYI there's a coverage gap from 00:30-01:00 UTC where me and Priya overlap with other commitments. Alex can cover comms in that window; recommend we set pager to route to Alex as primary during that 30m.
Alex: done — adjusted rotation. Also left a note in the oncall calendar.
Sara: small request — can someone add the link to the dedicated customers list in the incident? I can't find the up-to-date contacts quickly.
Priya: added contact list to the incident doc at 1934567940.
Alex: handoff checklist for incoming night driver (Mike):
- confirm autoscale returns to normal for 2 consecutive 5m windows
- verify no new alert noise from node controller
- check cost spike dashboard for unintended scale-ups
- if degraded still, escalate to infra-runtime pager and start long-lived mitigation (node pool resizing + quota limit)
Mike: copy. I'll take full driver at 23:00 (1934568600). If no major regressions I'll update 'resolved' when the queue stays <5 for 3 windows.
Alex: thanks team. Comms owner during 22:30-23:00 = Alex. Driver during 22:30-23:00 = Priya. Post-23:00 driver = Mike, comms fallback = Sara.
IncidentBot: Reminder: please update the incident status field when ownership changes to keep routing accurate.
Alex: closing handoff — ping me if anything changes. I'll post the final update at 23:15 or when we hit steady state. :white_check_mark:
